analysis.title: GS Sector Specialists: U.S. Industrials & Materials (Fed, PWR, AAL, LUV, AYI), 1 Oct 2026
key_insights: Industrials closed on the lows on 9/30, down 125bps, and materials fell 80bps, both well behind the broader market. Technology and energy led, healthcare lagged. Defense and data center names outperformed, while airlines, transports and autos fell.
Industrials finished September down 465bps and materials down 750bps. The desk notes seasonality historically improves into year end.
Most-asked names on 9/30: GM and F weakness, BA fade, FDXF continued weakness, AIR on day 2 of downside after its deal, strength in CGNX, KEYS, ROK, HON and AYI, and ITW down 3% on day 2 of weakness.

Pre-market on 10/1: US S&P futures up modestly, helped by MU's bullish forecast the night before. Japan +330bps, KOSPI +195bps, France -120bps on its budget reveal. Brent back above $100, WTI $92 (+200bps), corn near $5 after the WASDE update, 10-year at a local high of 5.31%, DXY near 102, Bitcoin flat at $83.7k.

Privo on risk: Nasdaq is near its highs and the market still feels underexposed. Micro is bullish against an ugly macro backdrop (credit and rates make broad beta difficult), AI is leading, Europe and the Russell lag, and vol hedges are relatively cheap. Stable rates would let AI keep lifting the index.

Privo argues that if productivity growth resembles the late 1990s, equities can tolerate higher real rates than most expect, but not uniformly. Small caps, lower-quality balance sheets and the consumer are hurt.

Corteva began trading as separate Corteva and Vylor companies on 10/1 with no when-issued trading. Feedback was to watch from the sidelines, with more interest in Vylor and debate on multiples for both.

AYI fiscal Q4 beat slightly: EPS $5.77 vs $5.57 consensus, revenue in line at $1.24bn, EBIT $233mm vs $231mm. ABL sales fell y/y but were about in line, and gross margin was 50.2% vs 49.8% consensus. Fiscal 2027 guidance is the next item to check.

GS economics (GIR) now sees an October hike as unlikely after August core PCE rose 0.25% m/m, below expectations, with y/y at 3.01%, well below expectations. The second hike in its forecast moves to December, and it sees a strong chance the FOMC concludes more hikes are unnecessary.
GS expects Q4/Q4 core PCE of 3.0%, well below the median FOMC participant's 3.4%. Comments from NY Fed President Williams on 9/30 also contributed to the view.

Q2 real GDP was revised up 0.7pp to +2.2% q/q annualized in the third release, and 2026Q1 was revised up 0.4pp to +2.5%. The savings rate was revised up significantly to 4.1% in August. The goods trade deficit widened more than expected. GS cut its Q3 GDP tracking estimate by 0.1pp to +3.3%.
GS Conviction List Directors Cut adds AMZN, BURL, HII, JCI and OXY, and removes APD, COP, GLNG, LOAR and TSN.

Airline field trip (AAL, LUV): both companies reported continued demand strength despite higher fares in response to much higher fuel, and Southwest flagged strong September trends. Both are assessing capacity, with December schedule changes possible but October and November hard to change.

If fuel stays high, AAL and LUV management said 2027 growth plans could face downside risk, which GS expects across the industry. Both are upbeat on longer-term margin expansion driven by revenue initiatives such as product, loyalty and network.

GS is constructive on PWR (Quanta) after a 9/30 lunch with management, seeing growth beyond the guided 7-10% organic CAGR through 2030 from transmission and distribution build-out and data centers. It reiterates Buy, citing the integrated model and pre-fabrication as margin drivers.

sector_views.rationale: The sector fell 465bps in September and closed on its lows on 9/30. The desk notes seasonality historically improves into year end.
Demand held despite higher fares, but fuel is far higher and management teams flag possible 2027 growth cuts if it persists. Margin expansion is expected over the longer term.
AI is leading the market and MU's bullish forecast is lifting pre-market sentiment.

earnings_insights: AYI fiscal Q4 reported 10/1: EPS $5.77 vs consensus $5.57, revenue $1.24bn in line, EBIT $233mm vs consensus $231mm. ABL sales fell y/y but were about in line with consensus. ABL gross margin was 50.2% vs 49.8% consensus. Fiscal 2027 guidance is pending.
MU gave a bullish forecast on the evening of 9/30 that lifted tech shares pre-market. The report gives no figures.
AIR reported post-market 9/29 and fell for a second day on 9/30 after the deal. The report gives no figures.
AAL and LUV said demand stayed strong despite higher fares, and Southwest flagged strong September trends. Both flag possible downside to 2027 growth plans if fuel stays high.
